title: Harimoto comes from two games down to beat Li Tianyang for Asian Championships title
standfirst: Japan's world No 3 lost the first two games of the men's singles final in Tashkent, then won the next three to deny China a clean sweep of the men's events.
body: Tomokazu Harimoto is the Asian men's singles champion after coming from two games down to beat Li Tianyang in Tashkent on Sunday. Li won the opening game 11-1 and edged the second 11-9, but Harimoto took the next three 11-7, 11-8, 11-7.

His route to the final had been far smoother. He beat China's Wen Ruibo 3-0 in the semi-finals, conceding no more than seven points in any game. Li needed five games to get past Taiwan's Kuo Guan-hong in the other semi-final, taking the decider 11-6 after Kuo had won the first game 13-11.

Harimoto's win denied China a clean sweep of the men's events. Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng won the men's doubles, beating their compatriots Wen Ruibo and Yuan Licen 3-1, and China's men had retained their team title earlier in the week with a 3-0 win over South Korea.

China and Japan shared all seven titles, four to three. Japan's other wins came in the women's team event and the mixed doubles, where Miwa Harimoto, Tomokazu's sister, partnered the world No 1, Sora Matsushima. China's Chen Yi beat Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the women's singles final, and Kuai Man and Wang Yidi won the women's doubles.

Harimoto went into the week ranked third in the world, behind Matsushima and France's Félix Lebrun. The championships, held from 19 to 25 October, also decided Asian qualifying places for next year's World Championships in Astana.
His next test comes quickly. WTT Champions Montpellier starts on Tuesday, with most of the men's top 10 entered but without the injured Wang Chuqin.
